- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive (sentiment > 0.5) — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or neutral (sentiment < 0.5) — model fails to capture downward pressure.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; adjust forecasts downward if sentiment drops sharply within 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if price has been rising for 5+ days, model often overpredicts further gains; reduce forecast slope after 5-day uptrend.
- Lagged sentiment effect: if sentiment was high 3–7 days ago, model should adjust downward to reflect delayed market reaction.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in early cycles — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for each 3-day lag from recent peak.
